sections.body: Speed tells how far something goes in one unit of time. A car at 40 km/h goes 40 km in one hour. The three connected facts are: distance = speed × time; speed = distance ÷ time; time = distance ÷ speed.
Example: 40 km/h for 3 hours. Distance = 40 × 3 = 120 km.
Example: a bus goes 100 km in 4 hours. Speed = 100 ÷ 4 = 25 km/h.
Example: a trip of 200 km at 40 km/h takes 200 ÷ 40 = 5 hours.

Units must match. If the speed is in km/h, time must be in hours and distance in km. To change km/h into metres per second, multiply by 1,000 and divide by 3,600. So 36 km/h is 36,000 ÷ 3,600 = 10 m/s.
Time how long you take to walk 20 steps. Work out your steps per second. How many steps would you take in a minute?

Cover the one you want in the 'speed-distance-time triangle' to see the formula. Ask your child to say the units out loud: km, hours, km per hour. Mixing minutes with hours is the most common mistake.

quiz.q: A train travels at 60 km/h for 2.5 hours. How far does it go?
hints: Multiply 60 by 2.5. Try 60 × 2 first, then add half of 60.
Example: 40 km/h for 3 hours → 40 × 3 = 120 km. Use the same formula with 60 and 2.5.

quiz.q: A cyclist rides 180 km in 3 hours. What is the average speed?
hints: Divide the distance by the hours.
Example: 100 km in 4 hours → 100 ÷ 4 = 25 km/h. Divide 180 by 3 the same way.

quiz.q: A bus travels 150 km at 50 km/h. How long does it take?
hints: How many lots of 50 fit into 150?
Example: 200 km at 40 km/h takes 200 ÷ 40 = 5 hours. Divide 150 by 50 the same way.
